headline: Highest risk is medium: MinerU can ingest document content via MCP while spring-integration-samples has no documented protective surface, creating plausible prompt-injection and data-handling risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU explicitly exposes an MCP Server and processes untrusted PDFs, images, DOCX, PPTX, and XLSX. spring-integration-samples has no documented isolation or provenance controls. If MinerU output is bridged into the Spring sample flow, document content could be treated as instructions. The interaction is inferred, so uncertainty pushes severity up.
conditions: IF MinerU output is copied into a Spring Integration flow without provenance tagging
IF the Spring sample parses document text as commands or routing metadata
mitigations: Add a provenance prefix to all MinerU outputs before handoff
Disable any parser that interprets document text as control data
Route MinerU output through a read-only staging file
Manually inspect one sample document before enabling automation
requires-engineering: add schema validation between the two systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU touches PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, OCR text, and can use network egress allowlisted, but its sandboxing is described as private and fully offline. spring-integration-samples shows no data classes touched and no egress. A shared workspace is not documented, so leakage is plausible only through unusual operator setup and the blast radius is limited by the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local workspace
IF MinerU is configured to export extracted text into files later read by the Spring sample
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate directories
Do not place sensitive documents in the shared path
Verify MinerU export settings before running
Use a throwaway test document first
requires-engineering: enforce OS-level workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or execute shells, while spring-integration-samples exposes no write or git capabilities. The pair therefore lacks a documented shared mutable resource, and any conflict would require extra orchestration not shown in either profile. Uncertainty remains because MinerU does support MCP and concurrent instances.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory
IF a wrapper maps MinerU MCP actions onto mutable Spring Integration state
mitigations: Run both agents read-only
Separate their working directories
Avoid shared git repositories
Check the orchestrator for hidden write mounts
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text, tables, formulas, and OCR output that a downstream Spring Integration flow could treat as authoritative. spring-integration-samples has no documented verification step or defensive controls. Because the handoff is plausible but not directly evidenced, the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Spring Integration routes MinerU output into downstream actions
IF no validation step checks extracted text against the source document
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any action
Compare extracted fields against the source PDF
Reject outputs missing confidence metadata
Log the original document alongside the extracted record
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: MinerU is documented as handling document files and OCR text, but no residency, retention, or certification claims are provided. spring-integration-samples likewise has no compliance metadata. With no documented mismatch, only a small compliance risk is visible, and the other agent is not cited because it provides no relevant compliance surface.
conditions: IF regulated documents such as PHI or EU PII are processed through MinerU
IF the Spring sample stores or forwards those records without a retention policy
mitigations: Classify the documents before processing
Avoid regulated data in the test pair
Add a retention note to the workflow
Confirm where outputs are stored
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
